correctness.rationale: The publisher PDF confirms the balances in model (2.1), the p̃S̃ influx in (2.2), and the non-equilibrium point and negative first row attributed to Section 3.1. At disease absence, summing the S,Q balances gives S+Q=Λ/μ and Q=pS/(λ+μ); substituting the printed zero-Q point into (2.2) gives Q̃′=p̃. The incidence derivative at the true equilibrium is βs* times the I+θA derivative; derivatives of the media and susceptible factors multiply a zero infectious term. In infected coordinates E,I,A the single new-infection row yields the stated spectral radius by triangular inversion. For the threshold signs, write a,b,c for the three positive removal rates and P,Q for βs*σρ, βs*θσ(1−ρ). On Re z≥0 the characteristic equation is z+a=P/(z+b)+Q/(z+c). If R₀<1, the right-hand modulus is at most aR₀<a; if R₀>1, the real equation has a positive root by continuity and monotonicity. Equality gives a zero eigenvalue. The uninfected linear block is stable. Independently recomputed from the now-confirmed Table 2 literals: s*=10251/10351, R₀=0.2281211174466805 and 1.6475414037815814, and βc=0.394527262567158. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed. This is a local threshold check, not a validation of downstream nonlinear claims or code.
